concepts.title: The Parts of a Plant
concepts.explanation:
Find a real plant to look at — a mango plant, a banana plant, or even a tuft of grass. Look at it slowly. A plant has different parts, and each part has its own job, just as your body has parts with jobs: eyes to see, legs to walk.

Down at the bottom are the roots. They grow down into the soil. Roots drink water for the plant, and they hold the plant steady so the wind cannot blow it over.

In the middle is the stem. It stands up tall and holds the plant up. The stem also carries water from the roots all the way up to the leaves.

The green parts are the leaves. Leaves catch the sunlight and use it to make food for the plant. That is a wonderful thing: a plant makes its own food, and it does it with light.

Many plants also have a flower. The flower is the pretty part, and it is where new seeds begin.

Point to each part and say its name out loud: roots, stem, leaves, flower.
concepts.example: Point at a plant and name its parts in order from the bottom up: roots, stem, leaves, flower. Say what job each part does.

concepts.title: What Plants Need to Grow
concepts.explanation:
A plant is a living thing, so it has needs — just like you. But a plant cannot walk to find food or water the way a goat or a chicken can. It must get everything it needs from the place where it grows.

There are four things every plant needs to grow strong and healthy.

Water comes first. Plants drink water through their roots. In the dry season we must water them, or they wilt and droop.

Light comes next. Plants use light from the bright sun to make their food in their leaves. Without light they turn pale and weak.

Warmth is the third. Seeds and plants like to be warm. The warm sun helps a sleeping seed wake up and start to grow.

Soil is the fourth. Good soil holds the roots firmly and gives the plant food from the ground.

Water, light, warmth and soil — remember those four, and you know how to keep a plant alive.
concepts.example: Water a plant near your home. Then check that it is standing where the sun can reach it. You have just given it two of the four things it needs.

concepts.title: Planting a Seed
concepts.explanation:
Every big plant, even a tall tree, started as a tiny seed. Inside each seed sleeps a baby plant, waiting for water and warmth to wake it up.

Hold one dry bean in your hand. It feels hard and small and still. But a whole plant — taller than a cup, maybe taller than you — is folded up asleep inside it. A seed can wait a very long time, dry and quiet, until water and warmth find it.

Soak a bean in water overnight and it changes. A dry bean is hard. A soaked bean is soft and fat, because it has drunk up water and is beginning to wake.

Gently split a soaked bean into two halves. Inside you can see a tiny pale tip — that is the baby plant. Around it is packed food, which feeds the baby plant until it can make its own food with its leaves. A tough coat wraps around everything to keep it safe.

Now plant one. Scoop soil into a cup until it is nearly full. Poke a small hole with one finger. Drop the seed in, cover it gently, and water it. Put the cup where the sun reaches it.

Then watch each day. The root grows down first to find water. Then the shoot pushes up towards the light.
concepts.example: Plant a bean in a cup of soil and water it. Look at it every day and say what has changed. Which came first — the root going down, or the shoot coming up?

commonMistakes: Plants eat food from the soil.
Plants make their own food in their leaves using sunlight. Soil gives them water and a place to hold on.
Seeds need light to start growing.
Most seeds wake up in the dark under the soil — they need water and warmth first.
